title: Jasper and Corvus's Shimmering Lantern
markdown:
Deep in the Brackenhorn Range, where mountains tickled the sky and ferns shimmered under moonlight, lived a young wizard named Jasper. Hair the colour of toasted acorns, eyes full of questions. He loved to explore when the moon painted everything silver. His friend Corvus, a crow as black as midnight, talked a lot. Together they were always ready.

Tonight a special job. Cool air, damp earth, wild mint. “We need the shimmer-leaf herb, Corvus. It only grows under the fullest moon. Best sleepy-time potions: fluffy clouds and happy bumblebees.”

Corvus, on his shoulder, bobbed. “Shimmer-leaf! And look—a lantern for our quest!” A small round mushroom cap, silver swirls painted to catch moonlight, glowing just a little. Not a flame. Their special light. Jasper smiled. Corvus’s ideas were always fun.

Deeper, ferns like little green flags, dewdrops like tiny diamonds, moonlight dappled. Corvus spotted something else. “Ooh! A pebble! So shiny!” Fluttered down. The mushroom lantern tumbled into soft moss, glow dimming.

“Patience now. Let’s just find the herb.” Jasper picked it up, tucked it in his satchel. Cheerful light, just right.

Long swaying shadows. A round rosy face from behind a giant toadstool: Grimble, a goblin baker, apron dusted with sparkling flour, little boots thudding.

“Ho there, young wizard! Have you seen it? The mountain lantern? We need it back before dawn!” Floury hands wrung, round tummy jiggling.

“A mountain lantern, sir? We have this little mushroom one. For gathering herbs. We haven’t seen a bigger one.”

Round eyes widened. “That’s no mountain lantern! The village needs the big one. It guides everyone home when the fog rolls in. Like a friendly star. Without it, the little ones might get turned around on their way to the bakery, and my honey buns will get cold.” A quiet deflating sigh.

Corvus was tidying feathers, shiny pebble safe under a wing. He hadn’t taken a village lantern. He’d liked a stone. Grimble looked so worried. Little goblins a bit lost: a fluttery tummy.

Corvus hopped forward. “I did find a very bright thing! Round and glowed, and then I found the shiny pebble.” He nudged the mushroom. “This is it! It makes a little light!”

Grimble peered, then smiled kindly. “A lovely painted mushroom. But the mountain lantern is as big as a pumpkin and shines like the North Star. It hangs on the tallest peak. I thought perhaps you had borrowed it by mistake.”

Jasper understood. Not their herb lantern. The village’s guiding light. “Corvus, I think our mushroom lantern helped you think you had the important one. We need to find the real mountain lantern.”

Head tilt, a little sad. “I thought this was it. It caught the moon so nicely.”

“It is a lantern. You were trying to help. And we will help find the big one.”

A soft hoot, gentle as a lullaby. Aisling, the wise old owl from the oldest oak. “Who searches for light? The mountain lantern was caught by a playful gust. It tumbled a little way, quite safe, near the entrance to my oak. Waiting like a forgotten dream on a soft bed of moss.”

Grimble’s huge sigh of relief. “Thank you, Aisling! And thank you, Jasper. And Corvus, for your bright idea!”

They followed the call. Nestled among the roots: the village’s mountain lantern, big and round, light pulsing like a friendly heartbeat. Honey biscuits from Grimble’s apron.

He hugged it close. “Our beacon. Our way home.” Beaming. “Before I go, moon-baked biscuits. Sweetest honey and a sprinkle of happy thoughts.”

Under the moon they shared warm crumbly biscuits of honey and starlight. Leaves rustled a soft song. Grimble had his guiding light. The mushroom lantern went back in Jasper’s pouch, a little secret. On the highest peak the returned lantern pulsed a silver path that mirrored the moon. Their small one, tucked away, held a quieter kind of light: enough for herbs, and for home.
